title: Shaun Evans officiating first World Cup game after being cleared of making alleged White power gesture
content:
Shaun Evans is returning to the video assistant referee booth in Dallas after being appointed to help officiate New Zealand’s World Cup fixture against Egypt on Sunday night.

This is the Australian’s first match since he was cleared by FIFA, world football’s governing body, after being at the centre of a controversy over an alleged White supremacist hand gesture ahead of Germany’s emphatic 7-1 win over Curacao on June 14, which he denied.

As Evans posed for the broadcast camera, he was captured making an upside-down ‘OK’ sign with his right hand.

FIFA initially said it was aware of the incident but did not comment until its independent disciplinary committee concluded that Edwards had not breached its disciplinary code.

In a statement, Evans described it as an “involuntary, subconscious twitch” and that he was “unaware” he had done it.

“The coverage following this incident simply does not reflect who I am,” his statement, released the day after the game, added. “Of course, I understand how the gesture has been interpreted and I regret this.

“I want to be very clear and categorically say that I did not knowingly or deliberately make the hand symbol suggested.”

Although he was cleared on Monday, Evans had not been selected for any matches until being listed for the New Zealand-Egypt group-stage match in Vancouver.

The 38-year-old will serve as the assistant VAR to Mohammed Khamid.
